profile.summary: GENEB compares 40 genomic foundation models on 100 DNA sequence classification tasks in 13 functional categories, such as promoters, enhancers, histone marks, DNA methylation and splice sites. Every model is scored the same way: a logistic-regression probe trained on frozen sequence embeddings, in full-data, 10-shot and 1-shot regimes, with MCC as the main metric. It is meant for choosing a DNA model for a particular kind of task rather than for a single overall ranking.

summary_quotes.text: GENEB covers **40 models**, **100 DNA classification tasks**, and **13 functional categories**, including promoters, enhancers, histone modifications, DNA methylation, splice sites, and lncRNA.
Every model is evaluated with the same frozen-embedding protocol in full-data, 10-shot, and 1-shot settings.
so it can be used to choose a model for a specific setting.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: GENEB tests how much task-relevant information a pretrained DNA model's frozen embeddings carry. Tasks are binary or multi-class sequence classification problems in 13 categories: histone modifications (30 tasks), promoters (22), enhancers (8), DNA methylation (8), splice sites (7), lncRNA (6), mouse enhancers (5), TF binding (5), species classification (3), regulatory elements (2), virus or phage (2), coding versus non-coding (1) and chromatin accessibility (1). The authors argue that rankings change across categories and data regimes, so results are reported per task and per category as well as overall.

Model rankings change across biological tasks and data regimes. The overall leaderboard does not identify the best model for every use case.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The tasks are taken from nine earlier benchmark collections: the original and revised Nucleotide Transformer tasks, GUE, Genomic Benchmarks, the Plant Genomic Benchmark, iPro-WAEL, deep4mc, iDNA-ABF and iDHS-EL. Each task is one CSV with a sequence, a label and a train or test split. The released train and test partitions of the source benchmarks are used as published, without relabelling or resplitting. Tasks with more than 10^5 sequences are subsampled. The task data are pinned to one Hugging Face dataset revision in benchmark_spec.json.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: A submission is an embedding extractor that turns each DNA sequence into one fixed-length vector. The harness fits a logistic-regression probe (max_iter=1000) on the training embeddings and scores the test set, in three regimes: all training data, 10 examples per class and 1 example per class. Results are averaged over five fixed seeds (13, 17, 42, 123, 997). MCC is the primary metric; accuracy and macro-F1 are also reported. The leaderboard gives a micro average over all 100 tasks and a macro average, the unweighted mean of the 13 category scores. Encoders must not be fine-tuned on task labels. Evaluation is run by the contributor; continuous integration checks the submission file but does not recompute embeddings, and community entries are marked self-reported.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: Download the pinned task data with the repository's sync tool, write an extractor class for your model under harness/extractors/, run harness/run_GENEB.py (the README suggests --limit 5 for a smoke test) and validate the submission file it writes. The README commands use placeholder names for the extractor and model.

run_guide.summary: Download the pinned GENEB task data, run the harness on one model's extractor and validate the submission file.
prerequisites: Python 3 with huggingface_hub>=0.24, numpy>=1.23 and scikit-learn>=1.2, as the README and harness/requirements.txt give them.
An extractor module for your model under harness/extractors/, subclassing BaseEmbeddingExtractor.
A GPU is assumed by the README example (--device cuda).

steps.title: Run the harness
steps.shell:
python3 harness/run_GENEB.py \
  --extractor MyModelExtractor --module my_model \
  --name_model org/my-model \
  --model_id my-model-300m --display "My Model 300M" --params 300000000 \
  --data_dir ./GENEB_data --device cuda --limit 5
steps.explanation: MyModelExtractor, my_model, org/my-model and the display values are the README's placeholders: replace them with your extractor class, module and model. --limit 5 runs only the first 5 tasks as a smoke test; drop it for the full run.
